titulo.texto: Spanish Casino: A House Built on an Old Hospital

frase_gancho.texto: Isabel la Católica Street received that name in nineteen ten, and this Spanish house had already been waiting for it since nineteen oh five.

puente_narrativo.texto: Continue along Isabel la Católica toward Sixteenth of September Avenue, where you will find Boker House, a steel-framed building that housed a historic hardware store.

como_llegar.texto: Return to Isabel la Católica and head south, crossing Madero, to number twenty-nine, where a Spanish club built its home in nineteen oh five.

guion_corto.texto: Isabel la Católica Street did not always have that name. The Spanish Casino bought the land here in eighteen ninety-five. Back then the street was called Holy Spirit Street, after an old hospital that once stood on the site. The current name arrived in nineteen ten, during the celebrations of the Centennial of Independence. The club was founded in eighteen sixty-three. It opened this headquarters in December of nineteen oh five, the work of the Catalan architect Emilio González del Campo. Look at the eclectic facade, with motifs that range from the Arab to the Plateresque. Before it had a home of its own, the club passed through several palaces.

guion_largo.texto:
The Spanish Casino was born in eighteen sixty-three as a civil association of the Spanish community in Mexico. It was a meeting place for Spaniards and their descendants, and for decades it had no home of its own. First it occupied the Palace of the Counts of Santiago de Calimaya, which today is the Mexico City Museum. Between eighteen sixty-nine and eighteen eighty-three it was in the palace of the counts of San Mateo de Valparaíso. A club that kept changing palaces is a good picture of how social life moved through downtown in the nineteenth century.

In eighteen ninety-five, the club bought a plot of land on what was then Holy Spirit Street. The Hospital of the Holy Spirit and Our Lady of Remedies had stood there. It was founded, in the early seventeenth century, by the couple Alonso Rodríguez del Vado and Ana de Saldívar. Around eighteen twenty it was about to close, and soon afterward the building was sold and demolished to make way for the casino.

Construction began in eighteen ninety-nine, under the architect Emilio González del Campo, who was of Catalan origin. It was finished in nineteen oh five. In December of that year it was inaugurated with an assembly in the main hall, now called the Hall of the Kings. The club itself describes the building as the most mature phase of eclecticism in architecture. On its facade and in its interiors, motifs are mixed that range from the Arab to the Plateresque.

Then comes the fact that gives this stop its title. In nineteen ten, during the celebrations of the Centennial of Independence, President Porfirio Díaz visited that same hall. That year the city council changed the names of several streets, including the one that leads to this building, to honor Isabel la Católica. In other words, the street you are walking along took its current name when the casino had already been here for five years.

The building did not stand still. Between nineteen thirty-nine and nineteen fifty-one, a second structure was built at the back. It added a large hall, a dining room, a bar, a bowling alley, game rooms and an auditorium. Later, in two thousand three, a stained-glass window by the Mexican artist Kischi Hentschel was installed. It pays tribute to the Spanish Constitution of nineteen seventy-eight. Among the building’s most outstanding features is also the stained glass that covers the dome of the inner courtyard.

The library has its own history. It began in eighteen sixty-seven with about four hundred forty-six volumes. It was reopened in nineteen ninety-six under the name of Carlos Prieto and today holds about fourteen thousand volumes. It is open to the public on business days. The building also houses a restaurant serving Iberian cuisine. If you plan to go in, check the hours and the access conditions first, because it is a club with activities of its own.

This stop also helps you understand the geography of the foreign communities downtown. The Spaniards had their casino. Nearby, at the corner of Sixteenth of September, the German Boker family left its mark with its hardware store. Both houses were built in the years when the Porfiriato was opening the capital to trade and to outside investment.

To look from the street, notice the contrast between the sobriety of the wall and the details in stone and ironwork. You do not need to go inside to notice the care taken with this facade. It was a time when social clubs were also a way of presenting oneself to the city.

texto.Current building: work begun in 1899 and finished in 1905
texto.Style: eclectic, with motifs from the Arab to the Plateresque
texto.Key fact: built where the Hospital of the Holy Spirit once stood

texto.pregunta: Myth: The Spanish Casino is in a viceregal palace.
texto.respuesta: Reality: The current building is eclectic and was finished in nineteen oh five, on the site of an old hospital; the viceregal palaces the club used earlier were different ones, such as the Calimaya palace.
